instruction.text: Select the dry, yellow ground to learn more about heatwaves.

feedback.end: A heatwave is unusually hot weather lasting for 2 or more days. In the UK, we get heatwaves every summer. In this picture, the grass has dried out because of the heat.

instruction.text: Select the cracked, dry ground to learn more about droughts.

feedback.end: In this photo, the river has completely dried up because there has been no rain and a long heatwave. When there is a shortage of water, it is called a drought.

instruction.text: Find the fire to learn more about the effects of heatwaves and droughts.

feedback.end:
After long, hot periods of weather, plants become very dry and catch on fire easily. This can lead to huge wildfires.

In places like Australia, these fires can burn for weeks! In recent years, the UK has also experienced some wildfires as global temperatures keep rising.

instruction.text: Select the images of things that are affected by heatwaves and droughts.

feedback.end: Droughts and heatwaves can stop plants from growing and mean that animals don’t have enough to eat or drink. Wildfires also destroy the habitats of living things.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in the sentences about heatwaves, droughts and wildfires.

Extreme hot weather is a ((++threat benefit)) to animals because they can run out of food to eat and water ((++to_drink to_swim_in)).

feedback.finish: When we have droughts in the UK, we often have a hosepipe ban to help save water.
